summary_paragraph: An elderly male with a history of atrial fibrillation, COPD, CAD s/p CABG, and alcohol abuse was admitted after presenting with chest pain and found to be hypotensive with acute liver failure. Evaluation revealed markedly elevated transaminases and a positive acetaminophen level, consistent with hepatotoxicity exacerbated by recent heavy alcohol use. He was treated with N-acetylcysteine, antibiotics for right upper lobe pneumonia, and supportive care for alcohol withdrawal. His liver function improved, and he was transitioned to the floor before discharge to extended care. He was restarted on home medications, educated on avoiding alcohol and acetaminophen, and referred for outpatient follow-up in liver clinic, neurology, and psychiatry.
